newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude ends higher as supplies seem balanced.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude ends higher as supplies seem balanced.

text.p: NYMEX crude extended its gains Friday after rallying sharply this week on the perception that after months of surplus, supplies are balanced amid high refinery runs and less imports on the horizon.

"With a lot of the West African crude now heading to the far east and runs high supplies seem to like they may remain balanced for the next 20 to 30 days," said Pat Hughes, analyst with Chevron Corp in California.
June crude ended nine cents higher at $20.43 a barrel. June gasoline ended 0.39 cent a gallon higher at 62.89 cents while June heating oil settled 0.14 cent a gallon higher at 54.52 cents.

The U.S. Gulf was hit with a steady stream of crude imports in March and April, particularly crude from West Africa. But, Asian refineries have come out of turnaround and are absorbing imports that had been going to the United States.
Cash crude dealers said European demand is picking up as well, limiting the amount of imports of North Sea crude.
Meanwhile, the American Petroleum Institute said U.S. refineries were running at 94.5 percent capacity last week rising a full percentage point from the week before.
Refineries have stepped up gasoline production to ready gasoline inventories for the summer driving season.
Meanwhile, dealers said prompt crude was technically shaky after testing and failing for the fifth time since April 21 the $20.50 to $20.60 resistance area.
June crude rose to a session high of $20.55 and abruptly fell to negative territory amid a lack of buying interest. It then recovered modestly intraday.

"The quick 30 cent drop happened in a vacuum. There was a lack of liquidity suddenly," said a New York trader. Dealers also noted that although crude has benefitted from a more balanced supply level, prompt crude remained in a $19.50 to $20.50 a barrel range where it has been since April 21.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
